can_it_be_verified.verified_for_you: All 6 prefix values were checked this session and all 6 resolve to real content: 82f40a2cd188 -> backup-105522/chron.py (82f40a2cd1887d14…); afb1ca65047f -> disk + git HEAD (afb1ca65047f569…); 600b9a85adc0 -> disk + git HEAD (600b9a85adc0181b…); f0b31aa62d54 -> git b8c600c (f0b31aa62d54…); dc1420b0eb19 -> git 133f692/HEAD (dc1420b0eb1941dd…); a15322a0f856 -> disk (a15322a0f856cd7e…).
can_it_be_verified.why_that_is_not_verification: A 12-hex-character (48-bit) prefix is a MATCH-ABLE value, not a VERIFYING one. Collision resistance at 48 bits is ~2^24 (~1.7e7) for a second preimage — a determined writer of a mutable production file can construct a colliding prefix. The seal asserts integrity at a strength far below the sha256 it names the field after, and it names the field `sha256_before`/`sha256_after` while storing something else. That is a representation claiming to be more than it is — the exact law the spine seal itself declares: 'A representation may never claim to be reality itself.'
can_it_be_verified.second_defect: The engine entry's `sha256_after` (dc1420b0eb19) did not match the working tree at the time this reconciliation began, and matches disk in no case — see REC-1. The file was never committed in the state it held when the seal was declared.
can_it_be_verified.third_defect_timestamps: The seal's declared `created_local` = 2026-09-18T11:20+08:00 is contradicted by the file's filesystem birth time, 2026-09-18T11:03:14.955369476+08:00 — a 16-minute 45-second gap. Two competing creation times are recorded and this reconciliation does not pick a winner (see OPEN-1). The choice matters: at 11:03:14 the seal's values were true of disk (stale 15 min later); at 11:20+ they were already stale at write.
can_it_be_verified.the_block_that_IS_verifiable_and_sound: `self_reported_defects` is the seal's strongest component. It records that the gate's own self-test caught three false alarms the author had written into it, and that they were recorded INSIDE the file rather than quietly deleted. That is a falsifiable, self-incriminating artefact of real value, and it is the part of this seal a reviewer should read first. It is not, however, a hash, and it does not verify file state.

spine_seal_assessment.plain_finding: The spine seal is a LEGIBLE RECORD OF A PASS and an UNVERIFIABLE CLAIM OF INTEGRITY. It should not be cited as proof that any file is what it was, because at 12 hex characters it was not built to carry that proof, and at least one of its values does not describe disk. It should be cited as the record of which nine boundaries were checked, with which verdicts, and by what evidence — that part is real, auditable and useful.
spine_seal_assessment.not_softened: This is not a minor formatting nit. A hash field that cannot verify and a count field that is scope-imprecise give a reviewer the sensation of verification without its substance — the same FALSE_NAME defect class the sibling lane correctly upheld against A-FORGE :7071 elsewhere today.
